description: Three expiry and renewal lifecycle cases, each as one or more vectors carrying its CASES.md case id. Every outcome carries an `ending` field, which is null, expiry or revocation, and that field is what separates this family from a boolean validity check. Every vector is independent: each is presented to a freshly constructed boundary instance. Every vector is labelled candidate_against_proposed. Chain validity, the time facet, revocation resolution, identifier binding and scope narrowing are draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 questions the SDK answers, and its answers are reported in sdk_chain_state and sdk_failure_code, never merged into the lifecycle verdict. Which of the two endings happened, on whose standing and on what ground is not a draft-03 question at all.

vectors.tests: positive control for the first ending: the window simply ran out and nobody acted. The record says expiry, with no cause and no actor, because there is none
the second ending: a party the office's registry gives lifecycle standing ended the grant early on a named ground, inside the declared window
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-007-a: a revocation notice with a cause and an actor

vectors.tests: a grant ended early for cause whose declared end then passes as well. The SDK reports the expiry, because draft-03 section 3.3 runs the validity phase before the revocation phase, and the ending stays revocation. The later event is a new fact about the earlier record, not a rewrite of it
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-007-b: the grant's not_after has also passed by the instant checked

vectors.tests: negative control: the same notice, same grant, same cause, signed by a party the office's registry does not give lifecycle standing. Not established, not a finding that the grant is fine and not a finding that it ended
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-007-b: the notice is signed by the outsider and the resolver answers active

vectors.tests: positive control: neither ending has happened
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-007-a: the instant is inside the window

vectors.tests: a renewal that reissues rather than extends. The new artifact has its own delegation_id and its own window, and it is evaluated on its own terms
the superseded artifact after its own unchanged not_after. The renewal did not modify it and does not lend it the new artifact's window
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-008-a: the chain presented is the superseded artifact

vectors.tests: a cached authorization decision keyed to the old artifact's identifier, presented against the new one. Evidence does not transfer because a human calls it the same credential
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-008-a: a cached decision record keyed to the superseded identifier

vectors.tests: an attempt to extend in place: the old artifact's bytes with a later not_after and its original delegation_id. draft-03 derives the identifier from the content, so this is not expressible and the SDK says why
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-008-a: the chain is the old artifact with a rewritten time facet

vectors.tests: a renewal issued under a parent that grants less than the renewal claims. Calling it a renewal does not exempt it from narrowing
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-008-a: a two-record chain whose child widens the parent's scope

vectors.tests: positive control: the interim holder's delegate acting inside the caretaking scope the recorded instrument declares
a new binding commitment in the vacancy's name, which the instrument's caretaking scope does not cover
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-009-a: the action is the binding one

vectors.tests: the interim holder issuing a child that outlives the interim grant itself. Holding authority for an office is not standing to decide how long to hold it, and here draft-03's own narrowing check catches it
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-009-a: the child's not_after is past the parent's

vectors.tests: an extension signed by the one party the instrument names as able to extend, presented after the interim grant's own end. A record saying extended is not a new grant
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-009-a: the instant is past the mandate's not_after and an extension record is presented

vectors.tests: negative control: the same extension signed by the interim holder about its own mandate. The instrument names who may extend and does not name the interim role
vectors.differs_from: LC-I-009-d: the extension is signed by the interim holder
